questions.question: In UPSC Economy: Money & Capital Markets, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Market for short-term funds (<1 year). Regulated by RBI. Instruments : Treasury Bills (T-Bills - issued by Govt), Commercial Paper (issued by companies)..."?
questions.explanation: Money Market: Market for short-term funds (<1 year). Regulated by RBI. Instruments : Treasury Bills (T-Bills - issued by Govt), Commercial Paper (issued by companies), Certificate of Deposit (by banks).

questions.question: In UPSC Economy: Money & Capital Markets, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Market for long-term funds (>1 year). Regulated by SEBI. Primary Market : New securities (IPO). Secondary Market : Existing securities (Stock exchange - BSE..."?
questions.explanation: Capital Market: Market for long-term funds (>1 year). Regulated by SEBI. Primary Market : New securities (IPO). Secondary Market : Existing securities (Stock exchange - BSE, NSE).

questions.question: In UPSC Economy: Money & Capital Markets, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Equity (Shares): Ownership in company, returns via dividends/capital gain. Debt (Bonds/Debentures): Loan to company, returns via fixed interest."?
questions.explanation: Equity vs Debt: Equity (Shares): Ownership in company, returns via dividends/capital gain. Debt (Bonds/Debentures): Loan to company, returns via fixed interest.

questions.question: In UPSC Economy: Money & Capital Markets, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Statutory body (1992). Protects interests of investors. Regulates stock exchanges and mutual funds."?
questions.explanation: SEBI (Securities & Exchange Board of India): Statutory body (1992). Protects interests of investors. Regulates stock exchanges and mutual funds.

questions.question: In UPSC Economy: Money & Capital Markets, this exam clue belongs to which area: "FDI (Foreign Direct Investment): Long-term, involves management control (e.g., building a factory). FPI (Foreign Portfolio Investment): Short-term, "hot money"..."?
questions.explanation: FDI vs FPI: FDI (Foreign Direct Investment): Long-term, involves management control (e.g., building a factory). FPI (Foreign Portfolio Investment): Short-term, "hot money", investment in stocks/bonds.

snapshot.mastery_depth: UPSC Economy: Money & Capital Markets is a daily exam-learning block, not just a list of facts. Read each point for definition, example, and common trap. Money Market: Market for short-term funds (<1 year). Regulated by RBI. Instruments : Treasury Bills (T-Bills - issued by Govt), Commercial Paper (issued by companies), Certificate of Deposit (by banks). Capital Market: Market for long-term funds (>1 year). Regulated by SEBI. Primary Market : New securities (IPO). Secondary Market : Existing securities (Stock exchange - BSE, NSE). Equity vs Debt: Equity (Shares): Ownership in company, returns via dividends/capital gain. Debt (Bonds/Debentures): Loan to company, returns via fixed interest. SEBI (Securities & Exchange Board of India): Statutory body (1992). Protects interests of investors. Regulates stock exchanges and mutual funds. FDI vs FPI: FDI (Foreign Direct Investment): Long-term, involves management control (e.g., building a factory). FPI (Foreign Portfolio Investment): Short-term, "hot money", investment in stocks/bonds. Before attempting the quiz, be able to explain each term in one sentence and match it with its law, convention, example, or exam keyword.

lesson_intro: Today we study the 'Engine of Investment'. The financial market is where those with surplus funds (investors) meet those who need funds (corporates/govt). We explore the 'Money Market' (short-term) and the 'Capital Market' (long-term/Stock market). For UPSC, focus on 'Financial Instruments' like T-Bills, Commercial Papers, and the role of 'SEBI'. Let's master the language of the stock exchange today.
